hints: Write dV/dt=5000−kh² and use V=2500h to relate dV/dt to dh/dt.
Substitute h=20 and dh/dt=0.4 to find k, then simplify the rate equation to the displayed form.
walkthrough:
Express the volume $V$ of water in the cube tank with base $50\text{ cm} \times 50\text{ cm}$ in terms of depth $h$:
$$V = 50 \times 50 \times h = 2500h \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}h} = 2500$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}h} \times \dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = 2500\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t}$$

Set up the rate equation for the change of volume of water in the tank:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = \text{Rate in} - \text{Rate out} = 5000 - kh^2$$
$$2500\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = 5000 - kh^2 \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{5000 - kh^2}{2500}$$

Use the given condition that when $h = 20$, $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0.4$ to determine $k$:
$$0.4 = \dfrac{5000 - k(20^2)}{2500} = \dfrac{5000 - 400k}{2500}$$
$$0.4 \times 2500 = 5000 - 400k \implies 1000 = 5000 - 400k$$
$$400k = 5000 - 1000 = 4000 \implies k = \dfrac{4000}{400} = 10$$

Substitute $k = 10$ back into the differential equation and simplify:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{5000 - 10h^2}{2500} = \dfrac{10(500 - h^2)}{2500} = \dfrac{500 - h^2}{250}$$

hints: Separate dh/(500−h²)=dt/250 and integrate using the standard logarithmic form for 1/(a²−h²).
Apply h=0 at t=0, then set h=20 and evaluate the positive time to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Separate the variables in the differential equation $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{500 - h^2}{250}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{500 - h^2}\,\mathrm{d}h = \dfrac{1}{250}\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Integrate both sides using the standard formula $\int \dfrac{1}{a^2 - h^2}\,\mathrm{d}h = \dfrac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\dfrac{a + h}{a - h}\right|$ with $a = \sqrt{500} = 10\sqrt{5}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2(10\sqrt{5})}\ln\left(\dfrac{10\sqrt{5} + h}{10\sqrt{5} - h}\right) = \dfrac{1}{250}t + C$$
$$\dfrac{1}{20\sqrt{5}}\ln\left(\dfrac{10\sqrt{5} + h}{10\sqrt{5} - h}\right) = \dfrac{1}{250}t + C$$

Use the initial condition $h = 0$ when $t = 0$ to find $C$:
$$\dfrac{1}{20\sqrt{5}}\ln\left(\dfrac{10\sqrt{5} + 0}{10\sqrt{5} - 0}\right) = \dfrac{1}{250}(0) + C \implies \dfrac{1}{20\sqrt{5}}\ln(1) = C \implies C = 0$$
$$\dfrac{1}{20\sqrt{5}}\ln\left(\dfrac{10\sqrt{5} + h}{10\sqrt{5} - h}\right) = \dfrac{1}{250}t$$

Calculate the time $t$ to 3 significant figures:
$$t = \dfrac{250}{20\sqrt{5}}\ln(9 + 4\sqrt{5}) = \dfrac{25}{2\sqrt{5}}(2.887268) = \dfrac{5\sqrt{5}}{2}(2.887268)$$
$$t \approx 5.590170 \times 2.887268 \approx 16.140 \approx 16.1\text{ s}$$
